study_identification_part.si_4_title: Lifespan Normative Modeling of Brain Microstructure

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian Regression (HBR) was used with cubic b-spline basis set expansion with five evenly spaced knots for modeling the non-linear effect of age. The model used batch effect modeling for site (n=37 acquisition protocols) and sex (n=2), with random intercepts for each batch effect. The algorithm is implemented in the PCNtoolkit.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: The HBR NM framework is thoroughly described by Kia et al., but here we summarize the basic principles. Let be a matrix of the number of participants and covariates. We added age and sex as the covariates for the present study and we modeled the non-linear effect of age with a cubic b-spline basis set expansion with five evenly spaced knots.; Batch effect modeling for the site (n=37) and sex (n=2). Random intercept for each batch effect: site and sex.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: VillalonReina2024.pdf.md: Section 5. Normative Modeling with HBR, lines 249-263; media-1.pdf.md: Supplementary Methods, lines 517-519

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Four DTI (Diffusion Tensor Imaging) metrics were modeled: Fractional Anisotropy (FA), Mean Diffusivity (MD), Axial Diffusivity (AD), and Radial Diffusivity (RD). These metrics were extracted from 21 white matter regions of interest plus a Global-WM measure (mean across the entire ENIGMA-DTI white matter skeleton), totaling 22 regions per metric.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: For the Global-WM, the FA showed an inverted U-shaped trajectory, with a peak at 29 years of age. The three diffusivity measures (MD, AD, and RD) show a U-shaped trajectory, with minima later in life: at 37 years for RD, 43 years for MD, and 53 years for AD.; Figures S1, S2, S3 and S4 show the lifespan trajectories and percentile curves for each DTI metric for the 21 regions besides the Global-WM.
nm2_2_response_variable.location: VillalonReina2024.pdf.md: Section 2.1. Lifespan trajectories of brain microstructural metrics, line 121

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age was modeled with a cubic b-spline basis set expansion with five evenly spaced knots to capture non-linear effects. Sex was included as a covariate. The 37 different acquisition protocols were modeled as batch effects (random intercepts) along with sex.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We added age and sex as the covariates for the present study and we modeled the non-linear effect of age with a cubic b-spline basis set expansion with five evenly spaced knots.; We identified 37 protocols across the studies. For instance, one study - ADNI3 - used seven distinctive protocols. The 37 protocols were modeled as a batch effect for the Hierarchical Bayesian Regression.; Batch effect modeling for the site (n=37) and sex (n=2). Random intercept for each batch effect: site and sex.
